_comment: Dataset registry. Each dataset must declare provenance. 'status' may be seed | reference | indicative | loaded; a missing file is reported as 'missing' automatically.

datasets.title: Mountain-system study areas
datasets.source: Portal team — rectangular study-area extents drawn for filtering only
datasets.limitations: NOT official mountain-system boundaries. Rectangles overlap and include adjacent terrain. Replace with a documented boundary dataset (e.g. GMBA Mountain Inventory v2) before analytical use.

datasets.title: Reference settlements (district / tehsil centres)
datasets.source: Approximate town-centre coordinates compiled by the portal team from public gazetteer knowledge; to be replaced by OpenStreetMap place=* extract (scripts/fetch_osm.py) or PBS / SoP data
datasets.limitations: Small reference set of main centres only. No population figures loaded. Not an exhaustive settlement inventory.

datasets.title: Historical avalanche incidents (seed catalogue)
datasets.source: Seed records of widely reported events; each record lists the reporting organisation. Must be reconciled against NDMA / PDMA / GBDMA / SDMA records.
datasets.limitations: Highly incomplete. Coordinates are proxies, not impact points. Casualty figures are as reported and unverified. Absence of a recorded incident does NOT prove absence of hazard.

datasets.title: Highway & road centerlines
datasets.source: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) — generate with scripts/fetch_osm.py roads
datasets.limitations: Not yet downloaded. Basemap roads are visible on the map but not analysed until this file exists.

fields.name: Road name
fields.hazard_affected_km: Length whose segment midpoints fall inside mapped hazard zones

datasets.title: Mapped avalanche hazard / runout zones
datasets.source: Not supplied — requires a mapped avalanche path / runout inventory or terrain-susceptibility model output
datasets.limitations: Without this layer, settlement and road exposure cannot be calculated and is reported as 'Not assessed'.

datasets.title: Terrain susceptibility (DEM-derived)
datasets.source: Not supplied — to be derived from a documented DEM (e.g. Copernicus GLO-30) using slope 30–45°, aspect, curvature
datasets.limitations: Not yet generated.

datasets.title: Snow cover (satellite-derived)
datasets.source: Not connected — candidate source MODIS MOD10A1 / Sentinel-2 NDSI
datasets.limitations: No operational snow product is connected.

datasets.title: Glacier outlines — RGI v7.0, Region 14 (South Asia West)
datasets.source: RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023). Randolph Glacier Inventory v7.0. NSIDC, doi:10.5067/F6JMOVY5NAVZ
datasets.resolution: Glacier outlines as mapped in RGI v7.0; geometry simplified about 30 m, coordinates rounded to about 10 m
datasets.limitations: 37,562 glaciers in RGI region 14. Sub-regions are RGI classifications and include glaciers in India, China and Afghanistan. Nothing is clipped to a country border. Not a hazard inventory.

fields.system: RGI sub-region (Hindu Kush, Karakoram, West Himalaya)

datasets.title: Pakistan boundary, provinces, Line of Control and disputed areas
datasets.source: Natural Earth 1:10m (public domain): Admin-0 countries, Pakistan point of view; Admin-1 provinces; disputed areas; boundary lines
datasets.limitations: Pakistan's boundary follows Pakistan's official position. Jammu & Kashmir is disputed territory and is labelled as such; the Line of Control is shown separately. Province names updated to current official names; former FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Small-scale data, not for demarcation.

datasets.title: Glacier system boundaries — RGI v7.0 / GTN-G glacier regions
datasets.source: GTN-G (2023) Glacier Regions, as used by RGI v7.0. doi:10.5904/gtng-glacreg-2023-07
datasets.limitations: Official glacier-inventory regions (14-01 Hindu Kush, 14-02 Karakoram, 14-03 West Himalaya). They group glaciers for inventory purposes and cross national borders; they are not geological range limits.

datasets.title: Glacier system boundaries traced from RGI v7.0 outlines
datasets.source: Derived from RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023) glacier outlines (doi:10.5067/F6JMOVY5NAVZ), clipped to GTN-G (2023) regions (doi:10.5904/gtng-glacreg-2023-07)
datasets.resolution: Outlines merged within about 5 km, shrunk 3.5 km, simplified about 300 m
datasets.limitations: A reproducible envelope around each system's actual glaciers, clipped to its official region so systems never overlap. It shows where each system's ice is; it is not an official boundary and not a mountain-range limit.

datasets.title: Major named glaciers (RGI v7.0)
datasets.source: RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023), attributes glac_name, area_km2, lmax_m, zmin_m, zmax_m
datasets.resolution: One label point per glacier (inside the glacier outline)
datasets.limitations: Largest glaciers that have a name in RGI v7.0 (10 Karakoram, 7 West Himalaya, 5 Hindu Kush). Many large Hindu Kush glaciers are unnamed in RGI, so the Hindu Kush list contains smaller glaciers.

fields.name: Glacier name (inventory code removed)
fields.rank: Size rank among named glaciers in the system

datasets.title: Hindu Kush very-high release areas (terrain screening)
datasets.source: Hindu Kush avalanche-terrain screening run 2026-10-15 09:39 (NGT, rule-based): Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (30 m), MODIS MOD10A1 winter snow 2015–2025, GLIMS glaciers
datasets.resolution: 30 m analysis; every contiguous Very-high area of 5 ha or more, one point per area
datasets.limitations: Rule-based screening from permanent terrain factors (slope × elevation × aspect × shape) with approximate thresholds. It is NOT a forecast, has no time dimension and has not been validated against observed avalanches. Forest cover and ground roughness are not included. The score (0–1) is a screening index, not a probability. Points are area centroids; a centroid can fall just outside an irregular area.

fields.max_score: Highest screening score in the area (0–1, not a probability)

datasets.title: Hindu Kush screening tile summary
datasets.source: Hindu Kush avalanche-terrain screening run 2026-10-15 09:39 (NGT, rule-based): Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (30 m), MODIS MOD10A1 winter snow 2015–2025, GLIMS glaciers
datasets.limitations: Rule-based screening from permanent terrain factors (slope × elevation × aspect × shape) with approximate thresholds. It is NOT a forecast, has no time dimension and has not been validated against observed avalanches. Forest cover and ground roughness are not included. The score (0–1) is a screening index, not a probability. Tile area is derived as very-high hectares ÷ very-high share.

datasets.title: Snow outlook 2026-27: 36 stations
datasets.kind: Station points with seasonal forecast and 15-day window values
datasets.resolution: 36 ERA5-Land grid points (~9 km); 10 Hindu Kush, 16 Karakoram, 10 Himalaya
datasets.limitations: Seasonal statistical outlook, NOT a weather forecast and not a lead-time forecast. Hindu Kush and Karakoram forecast equals the 1990-2025 normal (no method beat normal by >1 %); Himalaya uses El Nino analogs (small skill). ENSO input (ONI 2.5) is set in the notebook and not verified here. Danger days use fallback thresholds (30 / 50 cm new snow in 3 days), not learned from observed avalanches; not validated. Timing inside the season is the 1990-2025 average. Data end 31 Mar: 1-15 Apr is not modelled and left empty.

fields.hNN: Expected HIGH-danger days (>=50 cm/3 d) in window NN
fields.sNN: Forecast snow allocated to window NN by average timing (cm)

datasets.source: Northern Pakistan snow outlook 2026-27 (NGT notebook run Northern_Pakistan_Snow_Avalanche_2026_27): ERA5-Land daily 1990-2025 (~9 km), ENSO analog / normal method per range

datasets.title: Hindu Kush snow outlook: nearest-station zones
datasets.kind: Polygons: area nearer to a Hindu Kush station than to any other, within 60 km, inside Pakistan
datasets.limitations: Seasonal statistical outlook, NOT a weather forecast and not a lead-time forecast. Hindu Kush and Karakoram forecast equals the 1990-2025 normal (no method beat normal by >1 %); Himalaya uses El Nino analogs (small skill). ENSO input (ONI 2.5) is set in the notebook and not verified here. Danger days use fallback thresholds (30 / 50 cm new snow in 3 days), not learned from observed avalanches; not validated. Timing inside the season is the 1990-2025 average. Data end 31 Mar: 1-15 Apr is not modelled and left empty. Zones only carry the value of their one station; they are not a gridded forecast.
datasets.source: Northern Pakistan snow outlook 2026-27 (NGT notebook run Northern_Pakistan_Snow_Avalanche_2026_27): ERA5-Land daily 1990-2025 (~9 km), ENSO analog / normal method per range

datasets.title: Hindu Kush terrain x snow outlook by window
datasets.kind: Screening tile centres with relative index per window
datasets.resolution: 60 of 98 screening tiles (those inside a station zone)
datasets.limitations: Seasonal statistical outlook, NOT a weather forecast and not a lead-time forecast. Hindu Kush and Karakoram forecast equals the 1990-2025 normal (no method beat normal by >1 %); Himalaya uses El Nino analogs (small skill). ENSO input (ONI 2.5) is set in the notebook and not verified here. Danger days use fallback thresholds (30 / 50 cm new snow in 3 days), not learned from observed avalanches; not validated. Timing inside the season is the 1990-2025 average. Data end 31 Mar: 1-15 Apr is not modelled and left empty. cNN = 100 x tile share of High/Very-high terrain x station high-danger days / maximum. A relative ranking, not a probability.
datasets.source: Northern Pakistan snow outlook 2026-27 (NGT notebook run Northern_Pakistan_Snow_Avalanche_2026_27): ERA5-Land daily 1990-2025 (~9 km), ENSO analog / normal method per range

datasets.title: Glacier outlines in the Pakistan study area — RGI v7.0
datasets.kind: Glacier polygons clipped to the study area
datasets.source: RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023). Randolph Glacier Inventory v7.0. NSIDC, doi:10.5067/F6JMOVY5NAVZ
datasets.resolution: RGI v7.0 outlines simplified about 30 m, coordinates rounded to about 10 m
datasets.limitations: Study area = Pakistan-administered area: union of the province and territory polygons of Natural Earth 1:10m (Pakistan view), including Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu & Kashmir. India-administered Jammu & Kashmir, Siachen and the Shaksgam Valley are outside it. 225 glaciers cross the study-area edge and are clipped; area_km2 stays the official RGI area of the whole glacier, area_pk_km2 is the inside part. Not a hazard inventory.

fields.name: RGI glac_name (most glaciers are unnamed)
fields.area_km2: Official RGI area of the whole glacier, km2
fields.area_pk_km2: Area inside the study area, km2
fields.clipped: 1 if the outline was cut at the study-area edge
fields.src_date: Date of the source imagery for the outline

datasets.title: Glacier outlines outside the study area (context) — RGI v7.0
datasets.kind: Whole glacier polygons not wholly inside the study area
datasets.source: RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023). Randolph Glacier Inventory v7.0. NSIDC, doi:10.5067/F6JMOVY5NAVZ
datasets.limitations: Context only, drawn in grey. Includes glaciers in India-administered Jammu & Kashmir, Siachen, China and Afghanistan.

datasets.title: Glacier-system envelopes in the study area
datasets.kind: System envelopes clipped to the study area
datasets.source: Derived from RGI v7.0 outlines and GTN-G (2023) regions; clipped to the study area
datasets.limitations: A reproducible envelope around each system's ice inside the study area. Not an official boundary and not a mountain-range limit.

datasets.title: Major named glaciers with study-area flag
datasets.source: RGI 7.0 Consortium (2023). Randolph Glacier Inventory v7.0. NSIDC, doi:10.5067/F6JMOVY5NAVZ, glac_name
datasets.limitations: in_study_area is false for glaciers outside the Pakistan-administered study area (for example Siachen and Rimo).

datasets.title: Pakistan study area and border segments
datasets.kind: Study-area polygon, outside mask, border split into international and claimed segments
datasets.source: Derived from Natural Earth 1:10m (Pakistan view) in data/boundaries/pakistan_boundaries.geojson
datasets.limitations: Study area = Pakistan-administered area: union of the province and territory polygons of Natural Earth 1:10m (Pakistan view), including Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu & Kashmir. India-administered Jammu & Kashmir, Siachen and the Shaksgam Valley are outside it. The claimed segment is the edge of Pakistan's official outline around India-administered disputed territory; it is drawn dashed, not as a settled border.
